title: Normalized derived comparison from a finite exact cochain model
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with $\mathcal A$ having enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Assume their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the total right derived functor $RG$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] below exist and that bounded-below injective resolutions compute it. Let $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Fix $r\geq0$, an additive functor $F:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Ch}^{[0,r]}(\mathcal B)$ whose degree functors $F^a$ are exact, and a natural chain map $e_X:G(X)[0]\to F(X)$ that is a quasi-isomorphism for every injective $X$.

For every nonnegative injective resolution $s:X[0]\to I^\bullet$, form $B_s^{a,b}=F^a(I^b)$ and use the total convention [def-sp-double-complex-total] $d_{\mathrm{Tot}}=d_F+(-1)^a d_I$. Let $c_s:F(X)\to\operatorname{Tot}B_s$ be induced by $s$ along the $b=0$ row, and let $b_s:G(I^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}B_s$ be induced by $e_{I^b}$ along the $a=0$ column. Both maps are quasi-isomorphisms. If $\rho_s:RG(X[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}QG(I^\bullet)$ is the resolution comparison normalized by the derived unit $\eta$, then
$$\lambda_X=\rho_s^{-1}\circ Q(b_s)^{-1}\circ Q(c_s):QF(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}RG(X[0])$$
is independent of $s$, natural in $X$, and satisfies $\lambda_X\circ Q(e_X)=\eta_{X[0]}$. Here $Q$ denotes localization at quasi-isomorphisms. The transpose of $B_s$, with its analogous total convention, is identified with $\operatorname{Tot}B_s$ by multiplication by $(-1)^{ab}$ in bidegree $(a,b)$; the comparison is the identity on both axes. If $g_1,g_2:I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ are chain maps and $h$ is a chain homotopy between them, then the maps of these total complexes have chain homotopy with bidegree $(a,b)\to(a,b-1)$ component $(-1)^aF^a(h^b)$. When $r=0$, $\mathcal A=\mathcal B$, $F=G=\mathrm{id}$ and $e=1$, $\lambda$ is the canonical identity on $X[0]$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), algebraic discrete-lattice input to the tame-boundary calculation; returned lattice proof steps 5-7 and rank-zero case of step 10; homology.tex Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), derived.tex Tags 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift) and 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic).

proof.text: Write $h=d_F$ and $v=d_I$ on $B_s^{a,b}=F^a(I^b)$. Naturality of the differential of the complex-valued functor gives $hv=vh$. With [def-sp-double-complex-total], every degree of the total is a finite biproduct: $0\leq a\leq\min(r,n)$ and $b=n-a$. For the transposed bicomplex the differential is $v+(-1)^b h$. The map $\tau$ with component $(-1)^{ab}$ from the original total to the transposed total is a chain map: for an $h$-arrow the coefficients are $(-1)^{(a+1)b}=(-1)^{ab+b}$, and for a $v$-arrow they are $(-1)^a(-1)^{a(b+1)}=(-1)^{ab}$. Its inverse has the same components. On $a=0$ and $b=0$ it is the identity. This proves the claimed transpose comparison and lets us apply an axis-augmentation result with either index as resolution index.

source.place: Total complex convention; signed interchange of the two indices

proof.text: For each $a$, $F^a(s):F^a(X)[0]\to F^a(I^\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Indeed put $Z^0=X$, $Z^{b+1}=\operatorname{im}(I^b\to I^{b+1})$; the resolution gives $0\to Z^b\to I^b\to Z^{b+1}\to0$. Exactness of $F^a$ preserves these short exact sequences, so the augmented complex $0\to F^aX\to F^aI^0\to F^aI^1\to\cdots$ is exact. The components $F^a(s)$ commute with $d_F$ by naturality and are killed by $d_I$. They therefore form the chain map $c_s$ with precisely the stated $b=0$ components. Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation], taking resolution index $b$ and remaining index $a$, to the transpose of $B_s$. Its hypotheses are the just-proved degreewise quasi-isomorphisms, nonnegativity and the vanishing of the outgoing differential on the augmentation. Step 1 identifies the resulting total map with $c_s$, because the signed transpose is the identity on $b=0$. Thus $c_s$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), applied with the second index as resolution degree

proof.text: Set $A^\bullet=G(I^\bullet)$. Naturality of $e$ for $d_I^b$ gives $F^0(d_I^b)e_{I^b}=e_{I^{b+1}}G(d_I^b)$, so its components give a chain map $A\to B_s^{0,\bullet}$. Since $e_{I^b}$ is a chain map from a degree-zero complex, $d_F^0 e_{I^b}=0$; hence its total inclusion is $b_s$. For each $b$, the required augmentation from $G(I^b)[0]$ to the $a$-complex $F(I^b)$ is exactly $e_{I^b}$, a quasi-isomorphism by the hypothesis that $I^b$ is injective. Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation] with resolution index $a$ and remaining index $b$. This proves that $b_s$ is a quasi-isomorphism; the sign on $a=0$ is $+1$, so its source differential is exactly $G(d_I)$.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), variant involving the other index

proof.text: Suppose $g_1-g_2=d_Jh+hd_I$. Define $H^{a,b}=(-1)^aF^a(h^b)$ from bidegree $(a,b)$ to $(a,b-1)$, with zero components outside the quadrant. Additivity gives $F^a(g_1^b)-F^a(g_2^b)=F^a(d_Jh+hd_I)^b$. In $d_{\mathrm{Tot}}H+Hd_{\mathrm{Tot}}$, the two vertical contributions have coefficient $(-1)^a(-1)^a=1$, while the horizontal contributions cancel: their coefficients are $(-1)^a$ and $(-1)^{a+1}$ and naturality gives $d_F F^a(h)=F^{a+1}(h)d_F$. Thus $dH+Hd=\operatorname{Tot}F(g_1)-\operatorname{Tot}F(g_2)$. The same additivity calculation without the total signs gives a homotopy $G(h)$ between $G(g_1)$ and $G(g_2)$. Homotopic maps have equal images under $Q$, since [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] also defines the localization through the homotopy category.

source.place: Total differential and degree-minus-one homotopy calculation

proof.text: Use the assumed injective computation with its specified unit normalization, not an arbitrary isomorphism of derived objects: $\rho_s=\eta_I^{-1}RG(Qs)$. The unit is invertible on the bounded-below injective complex $I$ by the computation hypothesis. Naturality of the unit [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] gives $\rho_s\eta_{X[0]}=QG(s)$. Steps 2 and 3 and localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] make every factor of $\lambda_s=\rho_s^{-1}Q(b_s)^{-1}Q(c_s)$ invertible. Naturality of $e$ gives the strict identity $c_s e_X=b_sG(s)$, whose only nonzero source component is in total degree zero. Consequently $\lambda_s Q(e_X)=\rho_s^{-1}QG(s)=\eta_{X[0]}$.

source.place: Unit-normalized injective computation assumed in the statement; naturality of the derived unit

proof.text: Let $u:X\to Y$, let $s:X[0]\to I$ and $t:Y[0]\to J$ be the prescribed nonnegative injective resolutions. By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists] choose a chain map $g:I\to J$ with $gs=tu[0]$ strictly. The maps $F^a(g^b)$ commute with both differentials, giving $T_g:\operatorname{Tot}B_s\to\operatorname{Tot}B_t$. Functoriality and naturality of $e$ give the strict squares $T_gc_s=c_tF(u)$ and $T_gb_s=b_tG(g)$. If $g'$ is another lift, [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy] applies with $\alpha=s$, target $J$, and $gs=g's$. Its hypotheses hold because $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $J$ is bounded below termwise injective. It gives $g\sim g'$; step 4 then gives $Q(T_g)=Q(T_{g'})$ and $QG(g)=QG(g')$.

The definition of $\rho$ and naturality of $\eta$ on $g$ give
$$\rho_t RG(Qu[0])=\eta_J^{-1}RG(Qt)RG(Qu[0])=\eta_J^{-1}RG(Qg)RG(Qs)=QG(g)\rho_s.$$
Apply $Q$ to both squares in step 6 and substitute this equation. Cancelling only the isomorphisms $Q(b_s),Q(b_t),\rho_s,\rho_t$ gives
$$\lambda_t QF(u)=\rho_t^{-1}Q(b_t)^{-1}Q(T_g)Q(c_s)=\rho_t^{-1}QG(g)Q(b_s)^{-1}Q(c_s)=RG(Qu[0])\lambda_s.$$
For $u=1_X$ and any two resolutions this says $\lambda_t=\lambda_s$ in the same Hom set $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal B)}(QF(X),RG(X[0]))$. For arbitrary $u$ it proves naturality of that resolution-independent isomorphism. This uses naturality of the derived unit [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and composition in the derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and no uniqueness assertion for a map merely commuting with $e_X$.

source.place: Unit naturality and cancellation of the two augmentation comparisons

proof.text: When $r=0$, $F=G=\mathrm{id}$ and $e=1$, the augmentation $e_X$ is $1_{X[0]}$. Step 5 gives $\lambda_X=\eta_{X[0]}$. The identity functor on $D(\mathcal A)$ with identity unit is the right derived functor of the identity on complexes followed by $Q$. Under the unique unit-compatible identification of derived functors in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], $\eta$ is the identity. Therefore $\lambda_X$ is the canonical identity, including for an arbitrary chosen injective resolution; no injectivity of $X$ is needed.

source.place: Identity right derived functor and uniqueness of its unit-compatible identification
